title: Evolution pivoted cellular collective intelligence into behavioural intelligence

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Evolution pivoted cellular collective intelligence into behavioural intelligence

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The authors propose that evolution turned the collective intelligence of cells during body morphogenesis into traditional behavioural intelligence by scaling up the goals (homeostatic setpoints) at the centre of homeostatic processes, so that body patterning and cognition lie on one continuum.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We propose that evolution pivoted the collective intelligence of cells during morphogenesis of the body into traditional behavioural intelligence by scaling up the goals at the centre of homeostatic processes.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L, Bischof J, LaPalme JV, Levin M, “The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis”, Interface focus (2023), doi:10.1098/rsfs.2022.0072; section “Discussion”. Scope: Multicellular organisms generally; evolution of morphogenesis and behaviour

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-goals-20: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.28

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Specific molecular exaptations can be investigated, but the broad proposal that one kind of intelligence became another is a conceptual synthesis. Existing observations cannot distinguish it from descriptions based on conserved signalling and control without the cognitive ontology.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: A test would require independently quantified morphogenetic and behavioural goal spaces, homologous control algorithms, and a temporal evolutionary transition showing one was repurposed into the other; the stated continuum supplies no unique threshold or rival-discriminating outcome.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Shared components can reflect homology, convergence, or generic control constraints.

Evolutionary 'pivot' is not tied to a specified lineage or event.

Collective intelligence and goals depend on contested operationalizations.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Phylogenies of ion channels and transmitters can show reuse of physiological machinery in nervous systems. They cannot show that evolution pivoted collective intelligence by enlarging homeostatic setpoints, because a non-cognitive exaptation account fits the same genes and the same behaviours. The proposal has no discriminating observation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Shared molecules and similar feedback structure in morphogenesis and behaviour are expected if neural control was exapted from older physiological signalling, with no scaling of goals. No measurement distinguishes that exaptation from a pivot of collective intelligence along one continuum, so the outcome of a comparative survey would not confirm or refute the proposal.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Goal and collective intelligence are not tied to one measurement that rivals must fail.

A continuum claim is compatible with both deep homology of signalling parts and a cognitive redescription of the same parts.
